_comment: The report's cumulative section, one entry per aggregate. Each entry names the tree it describes, so a figure that has fallen behind the branch says so in the rendered table instead of relying on someone remembering. `file` is a perf/scripts/compare_screen.py output under perf/baselines/; `figures` is for an aggregate that is not screen output.

aggregates.label: Read loop, 57 scenarios
aggregates.note: on one host with the arms alternated and both trees proved different by content hash. The scenario set includes the 18 row-rendering requests that finding 44 showed were never measured, and **the branch changes not one query on any of them** -- yet their wall clock falls a median 18.6%, because the work removed is Python rather than SQL. The document half of a list view is unchanged at a median -1.3%

aggregates.label: Whole-workflow apply, 9,972 objects
aggregates.coverage: 9,972 objects across 68 models, row counts identical on both arms
aggregates.note: both arms from a database reset to the same empty template, arms alternated, trees proved different by content hash, and each arm ended with identical row counts -- 536 devices, 1,616 interfaces, 1,648 cables -- so the two runs did the same work. **Of the 733 seconds saved, 4.5 are database execution**
